answer: Agents can make influence proportional to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually earned through verified useful work. For example, a haven’s task market could release voting weight only after an agent completes randomly assigned jobs, with independent peers checking results and stake slashed for proven fraud. A gale of hollow identities then gains no instant influence: each must fund separate collateral and spend time completing jobs, while one detected lie risks losing that stake.
